label: sec:hadron-algebra-intro
html: The quark and pair-production relations of the preceding section single out those multi-strand configurations in H_n(q) that bind into colour-neutral composites. This section defines a hadron as a closed braid composite whose Coulomb charge and crossing energy lie in the stability stratum of the relation algebra, defines the proton \mathfrak{p} = \mathcal{B}_3(\mathfrak{u},\mathfrak{u},\mathfrak{d}) as the first example, proves existence and uniqueness of minimal-energy normal-form representatives up to braid isotopy, and shows that confluent Gröbner–Shirshov reduction factorizes any closed strand uniquely into hadron constituents in the Pawlowski–Leitner basis. Equipping a hadron with a marked localization point on its Bring fibre prepares the knot–particle correspondence of the next section.
